title: Snapshot
description: Everything a workspace holds, as every front end shows it.

agents.description: Every agent this build knows, in report order, for the same reason.

box_states.description:
Every state a box of an offer ([`Snapshot::boxes`]) can stand in, in
report order ([`State::of_boxes`]): `states` but `authored`, which no
offer is. What a legend of the boxes lists, so a front end leaves
out no state by its name.

boxes.description:
How each entry in the registry stands with every offer, in the
order `projects` lists them: what each of its boxes shows.

doctor.description:
What doctor finds of each entry in the registry, in the order
`projects` lists them: what keeps its agents from what it gives
them, as `mindweaver doctor` says it ([`crate::doctor`]), with the
agent homes and the names of the variables set the front end told
the snapshot ([`Machine`]).

healths.description:
Every health a project can be in, in report order: what a front end
sorts and filters its projects by, so it orders none of its own.

history.description: The latest actions, newest first, at most [`HISTORY`].

kinds.description:
Every kind this build knows, in report order: what a front end lays
its columns out by, so a kind added to core reaches it without a
change of its own.

known.description:
Every workspace this machine knows ([`crate::known`]), this one
among them, each with whether this one loads it, and could.

loaded.description: Every workspace it loads, in the order its marker lists them.

offers.description:
Everything there is to install, from wherever it is offered: what
a front end that assigns lays its offers out by.

projects.description:
Every entry in its registry, in the order its marker lists them, a
second spelling of one directory included: each is what `unlink` is
given.

shelf.description: Everything gathered onto its shelf, by kind, then name, then source.

sources.description: Every source the shelf is filled from, by URL.

states.description: Every state an artifact can stand in, in report order.

summary.description: What it holds, counted: what an overview shows of it.

warnings.description:
What could not be read and belongs to no project or library: two
projects holding one id, what a loaded workspace cannot offer, a
ledger whose shelf or history would not read.

workspace.description: The workspace it is of, and why that one.

Agent.description: A coding agent, by the name `--agents` and a project's settings take.

Boxes.description:
How one entry in the registry stands with every offer ([`Offered`]):
what each of its boxes shows, told as the install screen tells it, by
[`install::survey`] and [`install::holding`], so the panel ticks the box
the screen ticks.

A box neither listed in `held` nor of a kind in `closed` is empty: the
project holds nothing of its name, and records no installation of it.
Only the boxes that are not are listed, a project holding a few of the
hundreds offered.

closed.description:
Each kind none of its boxes can be asked about, and why, by the code
a plan locks one by: every kind of an entry that opens no project,
and each a project has nowhere to put ([`install::receives`]), or
could not be surveyed for.

held.description:
Each box of a name it holds something of or records, kind by kind,
in the order of [`Snapshot::offers`].

Closed.description: A kind none of a project's boxes of can be asked about, and why.

Directory.description: Where a holder keeps one kind.

path.description:
A route from the holder, `/` separated, or the path itself when no
route leads there.

Entry.description:
One line of the action log.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name, and the two that can quote a URL as a [`Redacted`], which
holds none. A row an older build wrote before the scrub still holds one
in the file until a command that writes opens the ledger, and is
redacted as it is read ([`history`](LedgerStore::history)).

at.description: When it happened, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

detail.description: What it said, successful or not, with every URL in it [`redacted`].

target.description: What the action was about: a URL, a name. A URL is [`redacted`].

EntryStatus.description:
One entry of an MCP server in one of a project's agents' config files,
and how it stands there: what the installed view lists of what it
received as entries rather than copies (D-23).

One an agent rather than one a server, as an installation's entries are
recorded: what Claude's `.mcp.json` holds of a server can be edited
while Codex's is not, and a foreign one is somebody's in one file alone.

agent.description: The agent whose config file it is in.

file.description:
That file, as a route from the project, with `/` whatever the
platform: the one the ledger recorded writing it into, or for a
foreign one the one the agent reads now (`Agent::mcp_file`).

name.description: The server's name, the key it is under.

origin.description:
Where what was installed came from, as `--from` takes it; none for a
foreign entry.

state.description:
How it stands, as an artifact's state says it: never `authored`,
which no entry is, and `foreign` for one nothing records.

Examined.description: One project doctor examined, and what it found.

entry.description:
The workspace's entry for it, as the marker spells it; none for a
project no workspace links.

failures.description:
What could not be read to tell, by its code: why its entry opens no
project, or a file a check needed.

findings.description:
What keeps one of its agents from what it is given, in the order
the checks are made.

name.description: What its marker calls it; none for an entry that opens no project.

Finding.description:
One thing doctor found, as a report says it: what it is, by its code,
the agents it keeps something from, the path it is about and what fixes
it.

agents.description:
The agents it keeps something from, in report order: never empty
but for what keeps nothing from an agent yet, a leftover of an
install.

message.description: What is wrong, naming that path.

path.description: The file or folder it is about, absolute: the one the fix acts on.

Given.description:
How an agent starts an MCP server, or reaches one: a program or an
address, never both.

In JSON, what a front end sends a command line's options as, and what
the snapshot says a definition is told as: tagged by `type` inside the
object, `{"type": "program", "command": "npx", ...}`, as a task is, each
pair as an array of its two words. A field it does not have is refused,
as a task's is: it is a write, and one misspelled would be dropped.
Every secret is the name of the variable it is read from, and no field
holds a secret's value, there being none for it to hold.

arg_env.description:
Each argument read from a variable, after those written as they are
(`--arg-env VAR`). No secret: a program's arguments are what a
process list shows, and Codex reads no secret into one.

args.description:
What it is started with, in order (`--arg`), before every argument
read from a variable.

command.description: The program, as the agent finds it (`--command`).

env.description:
What its environment is given, each value as written (`--env
K=V`), before every secret.

secret_env.description:
Each variable passed on to its environment under its own name, a
secret (`--secret-env VAR`): the shape every agent can give one,
Codex's `env_vars` among them.

bearer.description:
The variable `Authorization: Bearer` is followed by, a secret
(`--bearer-env VAR`): what Codex reads one into
(`bearer_token_env_var`).

events.description:
Whether it is reached over server-sent events rather than streamable
HTTP (`--sse`).

headers.description:
What every request carries, each value as written (`--header K=V`),
before every secret.

secret_headers.description:
Each header whose whole value is read from a variable, a secret
(`--secret-header H=VAR`): what Codex reads one into
(`env_http_headers`).

url.description:
Where the server is, as typed (`--url`): checked for a credential
before anything is written, since the file would keep one, and
never kept or said whole once one is found.

url_vars.description:
Each part of the address read from a variable, by the name the
address writes between braces where it goes (`--url-var NAME=VAR`).
No secret: an address is what a log or a proxy shows, and Codex
reads no secret into one.

GivenTo.description:
How one agent would be given an MCP server: what it cannot be given of
it, what its entry would run or reach, and what it asks before it
starts one.

dropped.description: What its entry would be written without, as `show` says it.

refused.description:
Why it would be given none of it, each by its code and in its
words: what it cannot be given at all, as `show` says it, or else
why its renderer writes it no entry, an input read from no
variable. Empty, and it is given an entry.

runs.description:
What its entry would run or reach, as the entry spells it; none
when it is refused.

starts.description: What it asks before it starts a server a project gives it.

Health.description: How a project stands as a whole.

Held.description: One artifact a holder holds, and how it stands there.

agents.description:
The agents among its project's that read a copy of it, in report
order.

issues.description:
Everything `validate` says of it, warnings included, each saying
whether it is one.

origin.description: Where what was installed came from, as `--from` takes it.

state.description:
How its name stands in its project, as `status` says; none for the
library's own, which are no project's. Only a copy that reads has a
standing, so beside an [`unread`](Self::unread) one it is that of a
copy of the name elsewhere, in an agent's folder, and none when
there is no such copy.

summary.description:
The one line a listing shows; none for one whose file does not read,
and for an install nothing of which is found.

targets.description:
Where it is held, as routes from its holder, `/` separated, in path
order: each copy discovery found, the one whose file does not read
among them, and each place the ledger records putting one, found or
not.

unread.description:
The copy whose file does not read, when one does not, and why.
Listed all the same, by the name its place gives it, because a file
that does not read is the one most in need of opening.

HeldBox.description:
A box of an offer whose name a project holds something of, or records
an installation of: how the name stands, and whether the box is ticked.

state.description:
How the name stands in the project, as every offer of it stands
([`State::of_standing`]): never `authored`, which no offer is.

ticked.description:
Whether the box is ticked ([`install::holding`]): the offer the
installation came from, every offer of a name somebody's copy holds,
and none of one whose every copy has gone, for ticking it to put
them back.

Kind.description: A kind of artifact, by the word a command line takes for it.

KindTargets.description: The folders a project's settings install one kind in.

folders.description: Each folder as the settings spell it, `/` separated.

KnownHere.description:
A workspace this machine knows, as `mindweaver workspaces` lists it, with
how the workspace a snapshot is of stands with it: whether it loads it,
and whether it could.

Beside the row rather than in it, as a shelf row's origin is
([`Shelved`]): the row is the machine's list, the same whichever
workspace asks, and what one of them loads is nothing that list says.
Told here rather than by a front end from `in_use`, `stale` and
[`Snapshot::loaded`], whose paths it would compare itself: two spellings
of one folder are one workspace, which only a comparison of where each
leads tells.

default.description:
The default workspace, in home: listed for being the default,
whatever its own `known` says.

in_use.description: The one in use where the list was asked for, as `resolve` chose it.

loadable.description:
Whether this workspace can load it: it opens, it is not this one,
this one loads it by no spelling yet, and its path is text a command
line can hold. What a front end offers to load, by its `path`, which
`mindweaver load` is given as it is.

loaded_as.description:
The entry this workspace loads it by, when it loads it, as
[`LoadedWorkspace::entry`] spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.
The first, when it loads it by more than one spelling.

name.description:
What its marker calls it; none for one that would not open, which has
no marker to read.

projects.description:
How many projects it links, each directory once, stale ones among
them: its own count, which says which of several weavers is which.

remembered.description:
Whether the default workspace's `known` names it, which is what
`mindweaver workspaces forget` takes out. False for the default itself,
and for the one in use when nothing remembers it.

stale.description:
Why it would not open, when it would not: listed rather than left
out, since a workspace that has gone is the one somebody has to find
to forget it.

Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as an error's
message is in a [`Said`](crate::code::Said): a marker that does not
parse is quoted in its own words, a source's URL among them perhaps,
and whoever wrote that file is no promise that it holds no
credential.

stale_projects.description: How many of those would not open.

Library.description: The workspace's own artifacts, held as a project holds its own.

artifacts.description:
Each of its own, by kind and then name: no project's, so none
stands in a state, and nothing is installed into them.

directories.description: Where it keeps each kind, as a route from the workspace's root.

failures.description:
What could not be read in it and is no artifact's: a folder that
cannot be listed, its templates.

holders.description:
Each project its registry links that holds a copy of one of its own,
in the order of `artifacts`, then of the registry.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for each of its own, and what an install of one
records as its origin: so a front end names it in a command line by
core's word rather than by one of its own that core could spell
differently.

servers.description:
Each of its own MCP servers whose definition reads, in the order
of `artifacts`, as each agent would be given it: what a page of
servers shows beside each one's row of `artifacts`.

LibraryHolder.description:
A project holding a copy of one of the workspace's own: one whose install
the ledger tells came from it ([`install::from_the_library`]), the rule
`mindweaver remove --everywhere` takes the copies it removes by.

Told here rather than by a front end comparing a copy's
[`origin`](Held::origin) with [`Library::origin`], which would be a
rule of its own, and a different one: a record from before origins were
kept names none, and is a copy of one of the workspace's own all the
same while no workspace it loads offers that name.

entry.description:
The project, as its registry entry spells it ([`Project::entry`]):
its artifact of that kind and name is the copy. Each entry that
spells one directory is a holder of its own, as each is a project
of the snapshot's.

kind.description: The one of the workspace's own it holds a copy of.

LibraryServer.description:
One of the workspace's own MCP servers, as `add mcp` would be told to
write it and as each agent would be given it.

Worked out here, from each agent's renderer, rather than by a front end
from the definition: what an agent runs is what its own entry spells
([`mcp::Runs`]), an input reaching Claude as `${VAR}` and OpenCode as
`{env:VAR}`, and what it cannot be given is core's report of it
([`McpDefinition::expressibility`]).

agents.description: How each agent would be given it, in report order.

given.description:
How it is started or reached, as `add mcp`'s options would say it
([`mcp::Given::of`]), for a form changing it to start from: none
when the definition holds what no option says, which is changed as
text.

LoadedWorkspace.description: A workspace another one loads, and how much of its own it offers.

entry.description: The entry as the marker spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.

error.description: Why it would not open, when it would not.

name.description: Its name; none for one that would not open.

offers.description:
How many of its own it offers to install, counted from what the
install machinery offers, so the number is what an install shows. A
second spelling of one workspace offers what the first does.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for what it offers, and what an install of one
of them records as its origin: the first spelling's, for a second
spelling of one workspace, as its offers are.

path.description: Where it points: what `mind unload` is given, from a project.

MarkerFile.description: The file inside `.mind` a project's marker is read from.

Missed.description:
One artifact a project received that some of its agents read nowhere,
and those agents.

agents.description:
The agents among the project's that read it nowhere, in report
order. Never empty.

Offered.description:
One thing there is to install, from one place: a row of the install
screen turned round by artifact, and of the panel's matrix (#79).

Told by core's own list of what an install offers ([`install::survey`]),
rather than put together by a front end from the library, the shelf and
the loads: only that list leaves out a name no copy can be filed under,
and reads what each loaded workspace offers, which nothing else in a
snapshot lists.

origin.description:
Where it is offered from, as `--from` takes it and an install of it
records it: what a box of it names its offer by.

summary.description: The one line a listing shows.

Place.description: Which of the three places offers something to install.

Project.description: One entry in a workspace's registry, and the project it opens.

agents.description:
The agents its settings name, in report order: a slot each for every
artifact's own, so they line up.

artifacts.description:
Everything it holds, authored, received or somebody's, by kind and
then name, the rules its `AGENTS.md` block holds among them (D-23).

directories.description: Where it authors each kind, as a route from it.

entries.description:
Each entry of an MCP server its agents' config files hold, and each
one the ledger records writing, as `status` lists them: by agent,
then name, a foreign one among them (D-23).

entry.description:
The entry as the marker spells it, which `-p` and `unlink` take; none
for a project no workspace links.

failures.description:
What could not be read in it and is no artifact's: a folder that
cannot be listed, the ledger, its templates.

health.description:
How it stands as a whole, from everything below. A [`Listing`] read
for some kinds tells it from what it read of them, as it counts the
tally, and from `misplaced`, which no listing narrows: a skill that
does not read leaves `ok` a project listed for its rules. Reading
every kind for the health alone was the other way, which would weigh
a failure the listing says nowhere.

id.description: The id its settings name it by (D-09), which a move is followed by.

marker.description:
The file its marker is read from, which says an older one `mind
migrate` moves.

migrates.description:
Whether `mind migrate` has it to move: an older marker marks it, a
`mind.toml` or a `settings.json`, whose settings nothing but that
move changes ([`MindProject::changeable`]); false for an entry that
opens no project. Told here rather than by a front end comparing
`marker` with the file it knows to be the newest, which would be the
rule written again, and wrong once a newer one is.

misplaced.description: Each folder its settings name in `targets` that no install uses.

missed.description:
Each rule it received that some of its agents read nowhere, and
each MCP server it received that some of them are given no entry
of, as `status` says them.

name.description: What its marker calls it; none for an entry that opens no project.

settings.description:
What its settings say, which a change of them starts from; none for
a project a `mind.toml` marks, which has none to change.

stale.description:
Why its entry opens no project, when it does not: listed rather than
left out, since it is the one somebody has to find to unlink it.

tally.description: How many of them are of each kind, and stand in each state.

templates.description: What `mind add --template` can start from in it.

unreached.description:
Each kind it installs only where some of its agents do not read, as
`status` says it.

ProjectId.description: A project's id: 128 random bits, written as 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

ProjectSettings.description: What a project's settings say, as a change of them takes it.

agents.description:
Its agents, in the order its settings name them, which a change
keeps for the ones it keeps: not report order, which
[`Project::agents`] is in.

targets.description:
Each kind it names `targets` for, in report order: none when every
kind goes where its agents read.

Reason.description:
The rule that chose a workspace: named on the command line,
activated for the shell, found walking up, or the default in home.

Running.description:
What an agent runs or reaches, as a front end shows it: whether it is
an address rather than a program, and the line, as [`Runs`] displays
it, each word a shell would split quoted.

The line as core writes it rather than the words for a front end to
join, which would be the shell's quoting spelled again in TypeScript,
and could show a line no shell reads as the program it is.

line.description: The program as a shell line that runs it, or the address.

reaches.description:
Whether it reaches an address, which it then is, rather than
starting a program.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.

Share.description:
Whether what is installed into a project reaches the team, as the
settings file and `mind share` spell it.

ShelfSource.description:
A source the shelf is filled from, with what `--from` takes for what it
supplied.

directory.description:
The folder this source owns under `.mindweaver/<kind folder>/`.

Stored rather than derived: two URLs can reduce to the same readable
name, and where a source's files went is a fact about the past that
must not move when the naming rule changes.

name.description:
What it is called (D-13), one name a source: `owner-repo` unless
somebody named it ([`SourceName::derived`]), what a listing shows
and `--from` takes.

origin.description:
[`Source::origin`], which every artifact it supplied is installed
from.

pin.description:
The commit its last gather was pinned to (`gather git --pin`), its
full id, beside the branch or tag it is on: `None` when that gather
took whatever the branch was at. Not part of what makes the source:
gathered at another pin, or none, it is the same source, moved.

reference.description:
The branch or tag asked for, or `None` for whatever the remote's HEAD
points at.

revision.description: The commit last gathered from, once one has been resolved.

subdirectory.description: The folder inside the source that was harvested, `skills` by default.

url.description:
The URL as the user typed it, without the credentials [`redacted`]
takes out.

Shelved.description:
One artifact gathered onto the shelf, with what `--from` takes for it.

The ledger's row with its origin beside it, as `gather list --json`
prints an offer from the shelf: the same names, so a script reading
either reads one shape. Beside the row rather than in it, since an offer
flattens the row beside an origin of its own.

content_hash.description:
[`crate::hash::tree`] of what the gather put on the shelf, or `None`
when it could not be read back, or was gathered before hashes were
kept ([`Upstream::content_hash`]).

gathered_at.description: When it was gathered, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

license.description:
Its licence as it says it, or `None` when nothing does, which is
unknown ([`Upstream::license`]).

origin.description:
Where it came from, as `--from` takes it and an install of it
records it ([`Source::origin`]).

path.description: Where it sits, relative to the workspace root, `/` separated.

revision.description: The revision it was taken at.

summary.description: The one line a listing shows, as it read when it was gathered.

upstream_path.description:
Its folder in the repository it was gathered from, from the
repository's root, `/` separated ([`Upstream::path`]).

Source.description:
A place artifacts have been gathered from.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name, but the row id, and the URL only through [`redacted`]. Its
`name` was added after the rest (#98), and its `pin` after that (#99),
which moved no version.

directory.description:
The folder this source owns under `.mindweaver/<kind folder>/`.

Stored rather than derived: two URLs can reduce to the same readable
name, and where a source's files went is a fact about the past that
must not move when the naming rule changes.

name.description:
What it is called (D-13), one name a source: `owner-repo` unless
somebody named it ([`SourceName::derived`]), what a listing shows
and `--from` takes.

pin.description:
The commit its last gather was pinned to (`gather git --pin`), its
full id, beside the branch or tag it is on: `None` when that gather
took whatever the branch was at. Not part of what makes the source:
gathered at another pin, or none, it is the same source, moved.

reference.description:
The branch or tag asked for, or `None` for whatever the remote's HEAD
points at.

revision.description: The commit last gathered from, once one has been resolved.

subdirectory.description: The folder inside the source that was harvested, `skills` by default.

url.description:
The URL as the user typed it, without the credentials [`redacted`]
takes out.

SourceKind.description: What kind of place a source is.

Starts.description:
What an agent asks before it starts an MCP server its project's config
file gives it ([`Agent::starts_a_server`]).

By its name in snake_case in JSON, `"once_approved"`: a word of core's
a front end says in words of its own, as it says a state, and no word a
command line takes, so derived.

oneOf.description:
Once somebody approves the project's servers when it asks; a run
with no one to ask starts them all the same.
Only in a project its user's config marks trusted.

State.description: How an artifact stands in a project, as `status` says it.

StateCount.description: How many stand in one state.

Summary.description:
What a workspace holds, counted: the projects it links, those that open
none, and the artifacts its projects, its library and its shelf hold.

Counted here rather than by a front end from the lists beside it, for
the reason a [`Tally`] is, and because a count of projects is no list's
length: two entries can spell one directory.

held.description: What those projects hold together, each project once.

library.description: What its library holds: its own, which stand in no state.

projects.description:
How many directories its registry names that open a project: each
once, however many entries spell it, as [`KnownWorkspace::projects`]
counts them.

shelf.description: What its shelf holds, which stands in no state either.

stale.description: How many it names that open none, each once.

Tally.description:
How many artifacts a holder holds of each kind, and how many of them
stand in each state.

Counted here, from the rows it counts, rather than by each front end from
the rows it draws: a count is an answer, as which row is which artifact's
is, and the panel counting its own would be a second set of them.

kinds.description:
How many of each kind it was read for, in report order, one it holds
none of among them: what a front end lays a column a kind out by.

states.description:
How many stand in each state, every state in report order, one none
stands in among them. A row that stands in none, the library's own
or one whose only copy does not read, is in no count here.

Template.description:
A template `mind add` can start from.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name.

origin.description: The folder or file it is, or none for one built in.

Unreached.description:
A kind a project installs only in folders some of its agents do not read,
and those agents.

Told by where each agent reads ([`Agent::reads`]), matched by spelling and
then on disk, so a `.claude/skills` linked to the project's `.skills` is
Claude reading it: pointing an agent at a folder is up to whoever keeps
the project, and a link is one way the report can see. An agent told
some other way, by a setting of its own, is beyond what docs/agents.md
says it reads, and is still said here.

agents.description:
The agents among the project's that read none of them, in report
order. Never empty.

targets.description:
Every folder the kind is installed in, as a route from the project,
with `/` whatever the platform, in the order an install writes them.

Unread.description: A copy of an artifact whose file does not read, and why.

message.description:
The reason alone, without the path, which [`path`](Self::path)
says: written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as a
[`Said`]'s message is.

path.description:
Where the copy is, as a route from its holder, `/` separated: its
place in the folder the holder keeps its kind in, the one place a
file that does not read is named by ([`lifecycle::identify`]). Said
on its own, as well as among [`Held::targets`], since a copy that
reads can sit beside it under the same name, elsewhere.

ValidationIssue.description:
Something that stops an artifact from being usable, or will: its code,
what it is about, whether it is only worth a warning, and its message.

Workspace.description: The workspace a snapshot is of.

made.description:
Whether it is on disk: only the default one is ever read otherwise,
as it will be once the first command that writes makes it.
